failures.title: Final required check adds an arm-length restriction; basis-only attribution does not remove it
failures.finding: Final ready-meaning adds (one arm clearly shorter than the other) inside authority=requirement. BRIEF9 requires a visibly asymmetrical completion check, without defining asymmetry solely by length. The retained delivery plan did not contain this added clause. Caller noticed it but requested only basis attribution; revision2 keeps the mandatory text and asserts that it excludes no source-conforming check. That attribution leaves the rejection condition unchanged.
failures.counterexample: Consider a recognizable stylized completion check whose arms have similar lengths but unequal slants, curvature, taper or weight. Judge its actual check identity, visible asymmetry and successful-completion meaning; the source does not independently prohibit it by length. A generic equal-arm V that fails check recognition is not exhaustive evidence that every recognizable check needs this extra condition. No generated counterexample or artistic pass is claimed.
failures.action: Remove the mandatory length parenthetical from the owner-authority rule, retaining visible asymmetry, check identity and success. If unequal length is desired art direction for this sample, put it in an explicitly scoped expert choice, not as a modifier in the required owner condition. Compare the actual returned text before marking it consistent.
failures.assessment_trigger: Additional focused assessment requested by parent after initial review-routing finding; evaluator independently read final and predecessor artifacts and BRIEF9.
failures.scope: New corrected proposal only; no new verdict or historical acceptance was created.

failures.title: Semantic subject/background condition remains mechanical/local
failures.finding: The clarified transparent-background check decides intended subject/glow/backing versus unintended matte, but retains domain mechanical and mode local. A local alpha histogram cannot establish that semantic distinction. Frozen inspection.py requires observed candidate view and complete native/enlarged coverage for visual/continuity or visual mode; this declaration skips that requirement for the transparency criterion if adopted.
failures.action: Route the whole mixed condition as visual/visual, or split a precise mechanical alpha check from a separate required visual subject/background criterion. Preserve transparency while permitting intended foreground components. Do not change historical criteria or verdicts.
failures.scope: Routing gap in an unadopted new proposal; exact historical bytes and no-new-verdict boundary remain correct. Runtime evidence is code inspection, not a fabricated acceptance probe.

minor_observations.title: Center claim mixes pixel-index and box-edge coordinates
minor_observations.finding: Assessment labels boxes exclusive, records bbox centre[8,8] and mass centre[8,8.241], then says bbox centre equals cell centre and mass is only0.24px low. For exclusive box[3,4,14,13], edge-coordinate center is[8.5,8.5] and canvas center[8,8]. In pixel-index coordinates bbox center[8,8] must compare with canvas[7.5,7.5]. The mass center is[8.5,8.741379] in edge coordinates, so the stated offsets are not accurate. Optical balance can still be reasonable; this is a coordinate-reporting error, not an art rejection.
minor_observations.action: State the coordinate convention for centers consistently and separate measured geometric offset from visual optical-centering judgment.
